content: Two dominant open-source local-first vault architectures: (1) KeePass/KeePassXC-style: a single encrypted file (whole-database AES-256/ChaCha20 encryption, including metadata) with no server component at all — simplest, most auditable, easiest to reason about for a single-user local-only app. (2) Bitwarden-style: zero-knowledge client-side encryption where the server only ever sees ciphertext, client derives keys from master password (PBKDF2/Argon2id) and encrypts individual records before they touch storage. For this project (single-user, local-only, no sync in v1), the KeePass-style whole-vault-encrypted-file/DB model is simpler and appropriate; the Bitwarden client-side-encryption-per-record pattern remains the right template to migrate to when cloud sync is added later, since it generalizes cleanly to a client/server split.
